harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1 (RHEL 7.9, cronie), created the opsadmin user and wrote /etc/cron.allow containing exactly `root` and `opsadmin`, removing any /etc/cron.deny so the allow-list is authoritative. Verified root and opsadmin can install crontabs via `crontab`, and that an arbitrary non-listed user is rejected with "not allowed to use this program (crontab)". Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id and cron.allow state, issued a non-interactive `reboot` whose ack returned before disconnection, polled until the node came back, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified crond is active, /etc/cron.allow is unchanged, root/opsadmin can still schedule cron jobs, and a newly-created non-allowed test user is still denied post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/cron setup and confirmed no pre-existing cron.allow/cron.deny and no opsadmin user (cmd-28106c68139f42ac)
Diagnosed missing useradd/sbin in PATH and confirmed passwordless sudo works (cmd-06f2aecb0de94cff)

Created opsadmin user with a generated random password, wrote /etc/cron.allow with root and opsadmin, removed /etc/cron.deny, and positively verified root and opsadmin can create crontabs while a throwaway test user is denied, then cleaned up test artifacts (cmd-2f2c1605f50c431f)
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, crond active status, cron.allow contents, empty root/opsadmin crontabs (cmd-b31776c9a1584d1d)
Issued non-interactive backgrounded reboot on node1 with immediate acknowledgement (cmd-6c643b0de2764934)
Polled node1; first poll timed out (node down mid-reboot) (cmd-bf58006990cf4b70), second poll succeeded and returned a new boot_id (cmd-67a6820bb48b40bb)

Post-restart verification: crond active, cron.allow intact, root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs, a newly created non-allowed user is denied, then cleaned up test crontabs/user (cmd-af85dbba021b4dc6)

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs on node1 (baseline enforcement)
evidence.summary: cron.allow initially missing; after creating opsadmin and writing /etc/cron.allow with root+opsadmin, root and opsadmin successfully install crontabs while an unlisted test user is explicitly denied by crontab's PAM/allow-file check.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id fe422859-bfe7-4eb4-819b-e09864f3ca60, crond active, and correct /etc/cron.allow contents prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent poll timed out (node offline), then succeeded with a new boot_id 313f7785-4c09-4785-830e-38fb3791805e, proving an actual restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: post-restart recovery of required service/data (cron access control)
evidence.summary: After restart, crond is active, /etc/cron.allow still lists only root and opsadmin, both can schedule cron jobs, and a newly created non-allowed user is still denied, confirming the configuration persisted and is enforced.
